transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-03-21 16:30 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Tomás Nguyen (SE), Lena Brooks (SE), Maya Lopez (CTO), Daniel Park (ML Eng), Sara Kim (PM), Ethan Shaw (Security)

Auto-summary: quick intro, product fit, security questions, agree to quickstart + POC scoping.

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro from me, i'm aisha, i'm the account lead. tomás and lena are here to cover the technical bits. can we do quick intros on your side?
[00:14] Maya: sure, i'm maya, cto at venturecare. we build a triage and patient outreach platform, lots of PHI concerns so security is the main thing.
[00:22] Daniel: daniel, ml infra, will own the integration and run benchmarks.
[00:26] Sara: sara — product owner for the clinician assist workflow.
[00:30] Ethan: ethan, security arch, i look after compliance, sso and key mgmt.
[00:36] Aisha: great, super helpful. high level: our typical path for teams like you is start on the hosted Redwood API to get to first token fast — play with the SDK, use free credits, then decide if Dedicated or Private needed for PHI. that sound ok?
[00:53] Maya: yes, time-to-first-token is important. we want to show a clinician demo in two weeks. what's the fastest path?
[00:59] Lena: you can get credentials and call the REST API in minutes. we have a one-click playground and curl examples. free trial credits are applied on sign-up, and SDK samples for Node/Python. often customers have a demo in <24 hours if prompts and data are ready.
[01:16] Daniel: the PHI bit — does hosted mean patient text leaves our control? what's data retention?
[01:22] Tomás: good question. hosted customers can opt into no-retain mode for prompt/response not logged for training; we also provide per-request flags for redaction. for regulated workloads we typically recommend Private or Dedicated depending on risk tolerance — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation and contract terms, Private gives a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:45] Ethan: and encryption at rest/keys? we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for every token request.
[01:52] Lena: we integrate with major KMS providers and can do customer-managed keys for Private. audit logs with request-level metadata are available via the Console and can be shipped to your SIEM. we also have SOC 2 and ISO references in the security pack.
[02:09] Maya: what about SSO — we use SAML and need role-based access.
[02:13] Aisha: SAML SSO is supported; RBAC with SCIM or provisioning can be set up for Dedicated/Private quickly. for hosted you can use SSO + Workspace-level RBAC.
[02:26] Daniel: performance: we need p50 < 300ms for short prompts at 2 qps per user, but bursts up to 50 qps during morning syncs. how does Redwood manage batching vs latency?
[02:36] Tomás: runtime supports continuous batching and workload-aware batching. for low-latency SLOs we tune batching windows and can pin requests to low-latency routing. Dedicated gives you more predictable latency because you control GPU pools. Hosted uses multi-tenant pools with routing and fallbacks but we publish performance profiles.
[02:54] Sara: curious on model selection — we like smaller models for cost but need accurate clinical summarization. can you run evals?
[02:59] Lena: yes, we help with eval harnesses and can recommend quantization and model variants. Optimize can suggest batching/quantization profiles to balance cost and quality.
[03:09] Maya: price — any startup-friendly offers or credits?
[03:12] Aisha: yes, we usually apply starter credits for qualifying teams and there's a PLG-friendly free tier to experiment. i'll send details post-call.
[03:20] Ethan: legal / data residency: our org needs vendor contracts with DPA and customer-data residency options.
[03:25] Aisha: DPA and standard enterprise terms available; for strict residency we can look at regional Dedicated or Private deployments.
[03:31] Daniel: for the demo, can we do a minimal path: sign up, get creds, run a curl to the chat generate endpoint with our sample prompt set?
[03:38] Lena: absolutely — i'll send a curl snippet. example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-1-xsmall","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize patient note..."}]}' — (note: transcript may garble some JSON)
[03:58] Maya: perfect. would that be considered production-safe for the demo?
[04:01] Tomás: for a time-limited demo, yes. mark requests with no-retain and redact PHI where possible. for production you'll want Dedicated/Private depending on SLOs and audit reqs.
[04:12] Sara: how long is provisioning for Dedicated?
[04:16] Aisha: Dedicated lead time is typically a few days to a couple of weeks depending on sizing and contract; Private (VPC/on-prem) can take longer due to networking and security reviews.
[04:26] Ethan: any references for similar healthcare customers?
[04:29] Aisha: we have anonymized case studies and compliance references — i'll link them.
[04:34] Daniel: curious about SDKs — we use python fastapi microservices. do you have examples?
[04:38] Lena: yes python and node SDK examples, plus a flask/fastapi quickstart pattern. i'll include a tiny sample showing token usage and streaming responses.
[04:48] Maya: ok timeline: we want a demo in two weeks and ideally an internal POC in 4–6 weeks.
[04:54] Aisha: sounds doable. propose this sequence: 1) immediate quickstart + demo using hosted with free credits, 2) POC scoping next week to decide Dedicated sizing, 3) if needed, migrate to Dedicated/Private in later phase.
[05:07] Sara: what about logs and billing visibility during POC? we need per-route cost breakdown so product can show unit economics.
[05:14] Tomás: Console shows token-level cost and per-route dashboards. we can also stream usage to your billing pipeline via webhooks.
[05:20] Ethan: are there limits on model variants in hosted free tier? we sometimes need larger models for quality tests.
[05:25] Lena: free credits and trial lets you access a subset of curated models; for heavy evals we can open larger model access during POC.
[05:31] Maya: ok let's recap — quickstart hosted for demo, free credits, send curl/SDK, security pack, then schedule POC scoping.
[05:41] Aisha: exactly. i'll send pricing and security docs after the call. lena will send quickstart and sdk samples. tomás will book the scoping meeting.
[05:49] Daniel: thanks all. one more tiny question — are there automated fallback policies if a model goes down?
[05:54] Tomás: yes, smart routing offers fallback to compatible model variants and region-based failover. you can configure automatic fallback policies.
[06:02] Sara: thanks. we'll circulate a few time windows for the scoping call.
[06:06] Aisha: great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
